subject: ACME trial — intermittent streaming hiccups impacting SLA and demo
messages:
From: Jamie Lin <jamie.lin@acmetech.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: ACME Tech Platform Team <support@acmetech.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Streaming output stalls during trial demo — urgent

Dylan —

We started a scheduled demo of the ACME trial this morning (10:00 PDT) and saw repeated interruptions in the streaming responses. Symptoms: the model stream will produce tokens for ~2–10s, then pause for 5–15s (no tokens) before resuming; in a few cases the connection returned a 502. This is happening on websocket and chunked-transfer endpoints. Latency and 5xx rate spiked during the demo window.

Attached: a light capture of the client-side timing and a small server-side log bundle.

This is blocking the demo and looks SLA-risky — can you triage immediately? We can pause the demo if you need quieter traffic, but we need an ETA on a mitigation and whether you can route our trial to a more stable pool. Also please let us know if you want any additional traces (we can run curl -v or provide client pcap).

Thanks,
Jamie Lin
Senior SRE, ACME Tech
attachments: acme_client_timings.csv, acme_demo_notes.txt

Subject: FW: ACME trial streaming hiccups — request triage + quick mitigation

FW: thread from ACME (see below). Immediate asks for ops/eng:

Observations from preliminary look at the logs Jamie sent:
- Bursts of concurrent trial traffic (~200–350 concurrent streams) correlate with the stall windows.
- On the gateway we see repeated "upstream prematurely closed connection" and occasional "broken pipe" entries.
- Token emission resumes in chunks after the pause (suggests coalescing/flush delay rather than model compute stall).

Hypothesis: the problem looks like proxy / reverse-proxy buffering + gateway worker saturation under bursty concurrency. Chunked-transfer flushes are being coalesced (or delayed) when buffers hit threshold, causing visible stalls to clients. Websocket keepalive behavior may be masking the drop.

Short-term mitigation proposals (please action in priority):
1) Ops (David): spin up a small dedicated pool and move ACME trial routing there to reduce noisy neighbor effects.
2) Gateway config: disable proxy_buffering for streaming routes, reduce proxy_send_timeout and proxy_buffers to encourage smaller, more frequent frame flushes.
3) Runtime: enable continuous-flush execution path if available for their model variant.

If this looks right, Rafael can handle the routing change and David can push a gateway config change as a canary. I can coordinate with ACME on timing. Tessa, flagging for exec awareness — if this continues we should prepare the customer credit/runbook and comms.

Thanks,
Dylan

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: dylan.brooks@redwood.com, rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Cc: grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-03T12:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: FW: ACME trial streaming hiccups — quick findings and immediate mitigations

Team — quick findings after correlating gateway metrics and the logs Jamie provided:
- At 10:01–10:12 we see a sharp CPU increase on gateway workers handling the trial, and a spike in keepalive queue depth.
- Nginx error log excerpt: repeated "upstream prematurely closed connection" and "recv() failed (104: Connection reset by peer)" around the stall windows.
- Packet capture attached shows the server continues to send segments, but ACKs are delayed/absent during the stall; downstream we see bursts of small segments followed by a gap.

Immediate mitigations we can apply now (low-risk canary):
- Set proxy_buffering off for /v1/streaming/* routes and reduce proxy_buffers to 4 8k.
- Set proxy_send_timeout 10s (was 60s) and proxy_read_timeout 30s.
- Enable continuous-flush path on the model runtime to avoid large KV cache flush pauses.
- Spin up a 3x dedicated worker pool (Rafael) and shift ACME traffic.

I will push a canary config to one gateway instance immediately and monitor. I've attached nginx_pcap_1103.txt and a short log slice. Recommend a 1pm war room to confirm customer-visible improvement and next steps for a stable rollout.

Attachments: nginx_pcap_1103.txt, acme_trial_logs_1103.zip

—David
Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Jamie Lin <jamie.lin@acmetech.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: ACME Tech Platform Team <support@acmetech.com>
Date: 2026-11-04T09:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Streaming output stalls during trial demo — update after mitigations

Dylan / team —

Thanks for the fast turnaround. We verified the streaming endpoint after David's canary (proxy_buffering off) and saw a marked reduction in the long pauses — the token stream is generally smooth now. We still observed occasional 3–4s stalls under synthetic burst tests (200–400 concurrent connects), but nothing like the 10–15s pauses earlier.

Next asks from ACME:
- A short runbook describing what changed and recommended client-side retry/backoff behavior.
- Timeline for a permanent production rollout and whether you can commit to an availability target for our trial instance.
- Please confirm whether Redwood will provide any trial credit given the interrupted demo.

We can schedule a 30-minute follow-up this week to validate production rollout (we prefer early next week).

Best,
Jamie
Senior SRE, ACME Tech

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-11-05T16:04:00-08:00
Subject: Executive update and customer communication plan — ACME trial streaming incident

Team / Tessa —

Summary for execs and ACME (to approve before we send customer note):
- Root cause: gateway proxy buffering + worker queue growth under bursty concurrency caused chunk coalescing and delayed flushes to clients. This manifested as multi-second to multi-ten-second streaming pauses and a transient bump in 5xx errors during the demo window.
- Short-term mitigation: we applied proxy_buffering off on streaming routes, tightened proxy timeouts, enabled runtime continuous-flush; shifted ACME to a small dedicated worker pool. Customer reports significant improvement; residual short stalls seen only under synthetic extreme bursts.
- Permanent fix plan and timeline: implement gateway streaming-optimized defaults in canary (11/06), finish validation and deploy to prod (11/08). Follow-up: increase dedicated pool capacity for ACME if they convert to Dedicated.
- Customer remediation: propose a 20% credit on the trial invoice and a waiver of overage charges for the demo window. Draft customer note attached (mitigation_runbook_1104.pdf).

Requesting approvals:
- Tessa: approve the customer-facing note and the proposed 20% trial credit.
- Rafael / David: confirm production rollout schedule (11/06 canary, 11/08 prod) and that the runbook is accurate.

If approved I will send the customer communication with the technical runbook and the timeline this afternoon.

Thanks — I'll hold off on sending until I have Tessa's sign-off.

—Dylan
Technical Account Manager, Redwood Inference
